title: Florida County Dog Ownership and Census Change
text:
This page combines a county-level census view with estimated dog ownership for each year. Use the layer switcher in the upper-right corner to move through 2000, 2010, and 2020, or think of it as a simple play-through of the changing county picture.



2020 estimated Florida dog ownership: 6,400,000 dogs
2020 estimated households with dogs: 3,320,000
County map colors represent estimated dogs owned, while hover labels show both dog ownership and census composition.

title: Florida County Dog Ownership and Census Change
text:
Notes
This version uses a simple estimate to connect the census county totals with a statewide dog-ownership trend. The map is designed to show both the demographic changes and the evolving dog-ownership picture in one place.

title: Florida Census Demographics (2000–2020)
text:
Between 2000 and 2020, Florida saw significant demographic shifts across all major racial and ethnic groups:

Hispanic: Substantial increases statewide, especially in central and southwest Florida.
White (non-Hispanic): Decreased as a overall percentage of population in almost all 67 counties.
Black: Steady population shares in northern counties, with growth in select central and southern metros.
Asian: Steady percentage growth across major suburban and university counties.

Use the radio buttons in the upper right to toggle which demographic shift colors the map. Hover over any county to view the full 20-year shift for all four groups.
